summary: GLOBE is a two-year Erasmus Mundus master's in global change ecology and biodiversity management. You study at Universidad Rey Juan Carlos in Madrid, Bangor University in Wales and the University of Lisbon, with a summer school in Tlaxcala, Mexico. Up to 25 students are admitted, and Erasmus Mundus scholarships pay all fees plus €1,400 a month. The first stage closes on 4 January 2027.
meta_title: GLOBE 2027: Erasmus Mundus biodiversity master's scholarship
meta_description: GLOBE pays all fees and €1,400 a month for a biodiversity master's in Madrid, Bangor, Lisbon and Mexico. The stage 1 online form closes 4 January 2027.
covers: All participation fees for 24 months: tuition, registration, insurance and the summer school.
€1,400 a month for living costs, accommodation and travel.
Without a scholarship, participation costs were €9,000 a year for students from outside the programme countries in the 2026–2028 edition.
eligibility: A bachelor's degree of at least 180 ECTS in biology, agriculture or environmental sciences, forestry, earth and environmental geography, natural resources or an equivalent subject.
English at B2: IELTS 5.5, TOEFL iBT 72 or Cambridge B2 (160). Nationals and graduates of countries on the UK's majority English-speaking list are exempt; Ghana and Nigeria are not on that list.
Anyone who has held an Erasmus Mundus scholarship before cannot get another.
how_to_apply: Stage 1, 28 September 2026 to 4 January 2027: fill in the online form with your personal and academic data (GPA and grading scale), English scores, a link to a one- to two-minute video and two referees' contacts. No documents are needed yet.

Stage 2, January and February 2027: shortlisted applicants upload an apostilled or authenticated degree certificate, transcripts in English, English proof, a Europass CV, a signed declaration and, for degrees from outside Europe, a postgraduate eligibility certificate from your university.
Scoring: fit of your degree 10%, academic excellence 35%, CV 32% (you need 50 of these 77 points), then video 15% and references 8%.
You are told whether you are admitted and whether you have a scholarship, and have seven days to appeal or confirm.
watch_out: Stage 2 documents must match what you declared in stage 1. A GPA declared higher than your transcript shows means automatic rejection.
Your passport must be valid for the full two years of the programme.
Book an English test early: it must be at B2 by 4 January 2027.
documents: Stage 1: the online form, a one- to two-minute video link and two referees' contacts
Stage 2: authenticated or apostilled degree certificates
Postgraduate eligibility certificate (degrees from outside Europe)

faq.a: The stage 1 online form closes on 4 January 2027. Shortlisted applicants send documents in January and February 2027.
Madrid (Universidad Rey Juan Carlos), Bangor (Wales), Lisbon, and a summer school in Tlaxcala, Mexico, with the thesis at any partner.
